added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the helper's docstring states "the same instant is written ``...T04:00:00Z`` by one caller and ``...T04:00:00.500000+00:00`` by another", but those two spellings name moments half a second apart, not the same instant; the node's own evidence fragment states the same example correctly ("name moments half a second apart but sort the wrong way round"), so the docstring contradicts both the mechanism and the fragment and could lead a reader to think sub-second precision is the hazard rather than the spelling.

follow-on: the third entry to `_raise_repository_scope_conflict`, the `_raise_live_scope_conflict` facade, builds its claims with the default empty registered_at and launched=False and passes neither own_run_id nor own_registered_at, so the parsed-time ordering never applies at that seam and a race through it still withdraws the pair; pre-existing and carried from the prior review, and nothing in reckon/ or tests/ calls the facade today.

follow-on: the ordering still compares wall-clock registration moments, so it fixes the spelling hazard this node targeted but not clock skew — a later arrival from a host whose clock runs behind still ranks as the earlier one, and the run-id tie-break settles only exactly-equal instants.

follow-on: the rule remains first-wins with no fallback, so if the registered-first dispatch withdraws later for an unrelated reason (a budget hold, a backend ceiling, a crash) after the later dispatch already refused on ordering, the paths are left with no worker; the state this node removes is removed only while the winner survives its own launch.

follow-on: the manifest names no baseline_suite and no after_suite, only gate.log and negative-control.log, so the added-failure count derives as unmeasured rather than zero and the record cannot be reconciled against a base arm at a stated revision.
